instruction: I have a few things in my amazon cart. For each product type in it, buy the cheapest product and move the rest to the wish list.
notes: The cart contents are unknown a priori, so the problem instantiates a representative cart: two product types, one with 2 products and one with 3 (5 cart entries, quantity 1 each), which yields the 10-call reference plan. Static facts (cheapest ?p) and (product-type-of ?p ?pt) encode the ground truth that the agent discovers via amazon.show_cart (gated by (cart-known)); at runtime the agent determines the cheapest product per product_type from the cart entries' price and product_type fields. Moving to the wish list is only allowed for non-cheapest products and only before the order is placed; place_order orders everything still in the cart, so (in-cart ?p) together with (order-placed) means ?p was purchased (in-cart is deliberately not cleared by place-order). Because the per-product goal facts are ground problem objects, supervisor-complete-task's domain-level precondition carries the generic goal condition (order-placed); the per-product wish-list/cart conditions are enforced by the goal plus the ordering constraints (no moves after order-placed), so any plan reaching the goal ends with complete_task and has all conditions satisfied at that point. Cart quantities are assumed to be 1 (the evaluation requires ordered and wish-listed quantities of 1); no quantity updates are modeled. Payment card and address ids come from amazon.show_payment_cards / amazon.show_addresses; no address is created or modified.
